Master's Thesis

Master's thesis

Classical and Non-Classical Symmetry Analysis & Invariant Solutions of Some Modified Partial Differential Equations

Riphah International University, Faisalabad (2023–2025) · Supervisor: Prof. Dr. Zulfiqar Ali

Lie symmetryNon-classical symmetrySoliton–BurgersAllen–CahnStability analysisImage scrambling

Abstract

This thesis studies two nonlinear partial differential equations: the (3+1)-dimensional modified Soliton–Burgers equation and the (1+2)-dimensional modified Allen–Cahn equation. For the Soliton–Burgers equation, both classical and non-classical (conditional) Lie symmetry methods are applied. They give similarity reductions and a large family of exact invariant solutions, including periodic, polynomial and square-root-type solutions. For the Allen–Cahn equation, classical Lie symmetries are applied, giving a kink-type solution, which describes a smooth phase transition between v = 1 and v = 0, and an exponential-type solution. The Allen–Cahn work is then extended: the effect of the parameter C on the kink front is studied, and a phase-plane stability analysis of the reduced travelling-wave system classifies the equilibria and shows how their stability is exchanged as the reaction parameter λ changes sign, a bifurcation-type behaviour.

As an application, invariant solutions of the Soliton–Burgers equation are used to rearrange the pixels of a grayscale image. The scrambling follows a fixed formula, so it is deterministic and reversible, and the original image can be recovered exactly. Unlike chaotic maps such as Arnold’s cat map, it comes directly from symmetry analysis, which links PDE theory with image security.

Under review

Propagation of Dispersive Structured Soliton Dynamics in the Modified Regularized Long Waves Equation with Dispersive Effects via Advanced Computational Techniques

Shafiq, S. & Baloch, S. A.

Jacobi ellipticKhater methodSolitonsNumerical check

Abstract

Wave solutions of the modified regularized long wave (MRLW) equation, a model for small-amplitude long waves in dispersive media, are derived with the Jacobi elliptic function method and the Khater method. They include bright, kink, periodic and singular solitons, and for each one the conditions under which it is real are stated. The bright soliton obeys a simple relation between amplitude, speed and width. All solutions are shown as 3D surfaces and contour plots, and a numerical simulation confirms them and shows that perturbed solitons stay localized.

Comparative Analysis of Microtubules as Electrical Conduits in Cellular and Neuronal Functions: Lump, Lump-One-Strip, Lump-Periodic, Breather, and Invariant Solutions with Applications in Bioengineering

Baloch, S. A. & Shafiq, S.

Lie symmetryLump solutionsBreathersRLC transmission lineBioengineering

Abstract

Nano-ionic currents along microtubules are modelled as a nonlinear RLC transmission line, and exact solutions of its governing equation are found with Lie symmetry analysis and ansatz methods. They include lump, lump one-strip, lump-periodic and breather solutions. Lumps are highly concentrated packets of energy, and the periodic and breather waves describe bio-electrical oscillations. The solutions give parameter ranges where energy and charge keep travelling in spite of dissipation in the cytoplasm, with possible uses in bioengineering and nanobioscience.

Lie Symmetry Reductions and Computational Analysis of Exact Solutions for the (2+1)-Dimensional Generalized Benjamin–Ono Equation

Baloch, S. A., Shafiq, S., Siddique, I., El-Naggar, M. A., & Abdullaev, S.

Lie symmetryMulti-wavesBreathersBilinear method

Abstract

Exact solutions of the (2+1)-dimensional generalized Benjamin–Ono equation, which describes small-amplitude long waves on shallow sea surfaces. Lie symmetry analysis reduces it to ordinary differential equations that give invariant solutions. A test-function and bilinear approach then gives multi-wave, homoclinic breather and interaction solutions. The solutions are shown as 3D, 2D and contour plots, and include dark and bright solitons, kinks and anti-kinks.

Lie Symmetry Analysis and Lump Solutions of the (3+1)-Dimensional Modified Soliton–Burgers Equation with Applications in Nonlinear Wave Propagation

Shafiq, S. & Baloch, S. A.

Lie symmetryLump solutions(3+1)-D

Exact solutions of the (3+1)-dimensional modified Soliton–Burgers equation, a model used in soliton theory, fluid dynamics and wave transmission. Classical Lie point symmetries give similarity variables that reduce the equation to ordinary differential equations, and an ansatz approach produces lump solutions. 3D, contour and 2D plots show the physical behaviour of the new solutions.
